Reading the workspace

  1. Requirements definition
  2. REQ-G60-US-DD-02

Progressive brake pedal feel and predictable recuperation

Proposal
1, implement. Braking draws 37 complaint rows (28 usability: grabbing, poor modulation) and recuperation 13 rows asking for consistent engine braking and a full stop in one-pedal mode.
Horizon
H1. Brake-by-wire and recuperation calibration.
Domain
Driving Experience & Dynamics
Markets
US
Evidence level
B (the best level of the primary and supporting findings)
Status
proposed, version 1

Statement

Brake pedal response shall be progressive without an initial grab, and lifting off the accelerator shall decelerate the car predictably, with an option for one-pedal driving to a standstill.

Acceptance criteria

One row per market where expectations differ. Basis: evidence is a measured study value or a count; assumption is the agent's proposal for the product manager to set.

MarketMetricTargetHow measuredBasis
USBraking complaint rows<= 15 per 6 months (today 37)Customer feedbackassumption
USOne-pedal stopCar stops and holds without the brake pedal in the strongest modeFunction testassumption

    • i'm happy with the car in general, but it has some surprising problems or design flaws: 1. i am not able to permanently shut off the "start/stop" function, and that makes the ride feel uncomfortable. 2. i also can't lock in the "sync" setting for the heater/ac so it stays on or off, which is irritating. 3. the rear bumper appears a bit loose and makes rattling noises when i turn or go over bumps. when i tapped on it, i could hear rattling, so something inside seems loose or the way it is built is faulty. 4. when i'm stopped at a light and then pull away, there's a click from the front passenger side wheel area. the brakes are probably releasing, but it doesn't feel smooth. 5. while idling, the engine will sometimes shake the car in a way i don't expect. 6. right after starting and driving off, the parking assist usually doesn't come on for the first few minutes, even when obstacles are close. i notice the same thing in parking spaces.

      G60-2264 · Source A · US · ICE · Defect, Braking, Noise · G60_feedback_hackathon.xlsx, row 2,838

    • the car is really fantastic overall. it has the best ride of any vehicle i've owned, and i really like the acceleration. the level 2 driving *mostly* works very well, though i haven't really played with the self-parking yet. my issue with the self driving is that it reacts too slowly when another car moves into or out of the lane ahead. once a slower car pulled into my lane and then had to brake because of traffic. the bmw 550e kept going at a higher speed as that car merged, and when they hit their brakes my car had to slam on the brakes hard. i honestly thought i was going to crash, but luckily it didn't happen. the hybrid setup is great because it cuts my fuel costs a lot. the downside is that if the destination is a fair distance away, the car uses *all* the available battery to get there, so you can't then precondition the car for the drive back. while i did have the money to buy it, i still feel it's a bit on the pricey side, and that makes me less willing to recommend a somewhat overpriced car to friends.

      G60-3636 · Source A · US · PHEV · Defect, Braking, Malfunction · G60_feedback_hackathon.xlsx, row 4,562

    • 1. forward collision warning and automatic emergency braking this car is supposed to come with standard forward collision warning and automatic emergency braking, but those features basically do not work. i have contacted your technical support several times, and although they made some tweaks, the system still does not function. in june 2025 i brought the car in again for checks. the technical advisor, michael, rode with me and we tried different driving situations and maneuvers, yet the system never reacted at all, no warning lights, no alerts, no braking. i also tried it myself on i-25 at highway speeds, deliberately getting within about 5 feet of other vehicles, and it still failed to activate. the sensor area has been kept clean and clear, we have gone through all the settings and looked at the owner's manual, but the problem continues. i realize the collision avoidance is only meant to assist, not replace careful driving, but i got used to relying heavily on a similar setup in my previous lexus. i expected the bmw system to work at least as well and would like ongoing help to find a fix. 2. homelink garage door opener the second issue is with homelink. two of your technical advisors came to my home to try and pair it with my garage opener, but they couldn't get it to sync. later i brought in a professional opener technician from liftpro, who finally managed to create a connection, yet the homelink is still unreliable and only works now and then. most of the time when i come home, the car will not open the garage door. i end up parking, going in through the front door, and opening the garage by hand, which basically defeats having the integrated system in the first place.

    • Customer stated that in the regenerative braking mode, even the setting meant for slower braking makes the car stop too abruptly and he does not think his lights come on. Customer stated that on a trip, people behind honked when he slowed, he felt nearly hit, and will not use that mode again.

      G60-2622 · Source B · US · BEV · Difficult to Use, Brake Energy Regeneration / recuperation, Not user-friendly · G60_feedback_hackathon.xlsx, row 3,307

    • Customer mentioned they are not happy with how quickly the car slows when they lift off the accelerator, so they keep the regeneration at low. Customer stated that at times it switches back to the highest regen setting. Writer asked if the same profile was being used, and customer replied the same person could be driving.

      G60-2062 · Source B · US · BEV · Difficult to Use, Brake Energy Regeneration / recuperation, Not user-friendly · G60_feedback_hackathon.xlsx, row 2,592

    • Customer asked which setting to use among Adaptive, High, Medium, or Low. Writer used RVG to confirm what the customer was looking at. Writer explained that these options control the brake regeneration. Writer advised that Adaptive varies the amount of regeneration with driving conditions, while the other levels keep the regeneration at a fixed level.

      G60-3946 · Source B · US · BEV · Difficult to Use, Brake Energy Regeneration / recuperation, Not user-friendly · G60_feedback_hackathon.xlsx, row 4,945

    • Customer asked if using the turn signal would cause increased regenerative braking when approaching a corner. Writer advised that brake regeneration is not impacted by the signal itself, but can change based on how the brake pedal is applied and which engine is being used during the drive. Customer then asked if regeneration is strongest in sport mode, and writer advised that it is best in sport mode.

      G60-1340 · Source B · US · PHEV · Difficult to Use, Brake Energy Regeneration / recuperation, Not user-friendly · G60_feedback_hackathon.xlsx, row 1,675

    • Customer stated that with this EV he was surprised by how much the car begins to slow when he lets off the accelerator, and that this feels quite different compared to an ICE vehicle. Writer explained that a big part of that sensation is energy recuperation, or regenerative braking. Writer advised the vehicle starts converting kinetic energy and charging the battery as soon as the accelerator is released. Customer stated the explanation at purchase could have been better and that this new feel is going to take a little getting used to.

      G60-1291 · Source B · US · BEV · Difficult to Use, Brake Energy Regeneration / recuperation, Not user-friendly · G60_feedback_hackathon.xlsx, row 1,615

    • i've had a lot of 5 series bmw cars over the years. on this 2025 i wish the steering gave more road feedback, it reminds me of the very light power steering from when i was younger. i do appreciate how smooth it is on the freeway, definitely feels more upscale than my older ones. what bothers me is when i lift off the accelerator, the car hardly slows unless i actually brake, so there is almost no engine braking. i have both a 530 and 540 from the 2025 model year and they both behave that way, and honestly i can barely tell any difference in how they drive.

      G60-0792 · Source A · US · ICE · Difficult to Use, Brake Energy Regeneration / recuperation, Effect, power not OK · G60_feedback_hackathon.xlsx, row 987

    • Customer stated it was hard to get used to Adaptive Recuperation. Customer stated he normally expects the car to coast when he releases the accelerator, but in this vehicle it feels like it is braking when he expects coasting. Writer stated Adaptive Recuperation is designed to recover some of the energy that would be lost while the vehicle is coasting and use that energy to charge the battery. Writer stated that if the customer does not like Adaptive Recuperation, he can reduce the strength by going to the Apps menu, then Driving Settings, Drivetrain and chassis, Adaptive Recuperation, and selecting the desired setting.

      G60-2029 · Source B · US · BEV · Difficult to Use, Brake Energy Regeneration / recuperation, Not user-friendly · G60_feedback_hackathon.xlsx, row 2,551

    • Customer explained that the regenerative braking on the i5 feels quite different from the iX. Customer stated that on the iX, regen kicks in immediately when you lift off the accelerator, at any speed or in any situation. Customer stated the i5 instead uses adaptive regenerative braking, changing its behavior depending on the vehicle speed, surroundings, and location. Customer mentioned that at times the i5 will coast unexpectedly. Customer reported it has been challenging to adjust to how the i5's regenerative braking operates compared to the iX. Customer said it would be preferable if there were some way to fine-tune how the adaptive regenerative braking functions. Customer added that overall they do think adaptive regenerative braking is better, but it remains difficult to get used to after being accustomed to the iX setup.
